artifacts.summary: Confirms the reviser-agent handoff contract contradiction: a dispatch[] 'plan' row can resolve to reviser-agent (existing-plan admission rule) carrying orchestrator_mode:true, but reviser-agent.md has no handoff-writing section on either call path. Recommends direction (a): add a conditional handoff section to reviser-agent.md mirroring planner-agent.md, add a Handoff Writers table row in handoff-schema.md, and a clarifying note in SKILL.md's Skill-to-Agent Mapping table; no script changes needed.

memory_candidates.content: orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's resolve_agent() for the 'plan' op uses an artifact-based admission rule (existing plans/*.md -> reviser-agent, else planner-agent), bypassing command-route-agent.sh entirely. Both resolved agents feed the SAME dispatch[] array, and skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md's Move 2 dispatch[] loop is agent-agnostic: every dispatch[] row (regardless of which agent was resolved) gets orchestrator_mode: true and a handoff_path. When a phase's agent-resolution path is artifact-based rather than purely task-type-routed, check that every possible resolved agent actually has a handoff-writing contract in its own agent.md file -- the dispatch mechanism treating it as handoff-expected does not imply the agent file was ever updated to match.

docs/architecture/handoff-schema.md's 'Handoff Writers' table is the single declared authority for which agents must write .orchestrator-handoff.json. Its own 'Registering a new writer' note states adding a writer is a table-row-only change (no script-side change needed), because orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh deliberately uses a dispatch-derived (phase-keyed), not agent-name-keyed, handoff-expectation check (see its own 'D1' design comment) -- so closing a writer gap is an agent-contract + doc-table edit, not a postflight script edit.
